seo.metaTitle: Convert PNG to BMP - Free Converter, No Upload
seo.metaDescription: Convert PNG to BMP in your browser. The result is a 24-bit bitmap for Windows and old software. Free, no upload, no signup, no watermark.
seo.longDescription: Convert PNG to BMP re-encodes your image as a plain 24-bit bitmap — the uncompressed format that Windows, office software and older engineering and printing tools still expect. Every pixel is stored as is, with no compression and no quality loss from the encoding itself. A 24-bit BMP has no transparency, so transparent parts are flattened onto black. The conversion runs in your browser and the source file is never uploaded.
facts: Runs entirely in your browser: no upload, no server, no signup.
Writes an uncompressed 24-bit BMP: pixels are stored literally, no encoding loss.
No alpha channel in a 24-bit BMP — transparent areas are flattened onto black.
Free with no daily limit, no watermark and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: Drop the PNG into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Preview the result; transparent areas are flattened onto black.
Download the .bmp file from the Download button.

faq.q: What happens to transparency when saving as BMP?
faq.a: The output is a 24-bit bitmap, which has no alpha channel, so transparent pixels are written as opaque black. If you need transparency to survive, export to PNG or WebP instead.

faq.q: Why is my BMP so much bigger than the PNG?
faq.a: BMP is uncompressed: every pixel is stored literally, so a 1000 by 1000 picture takes about 3 MB regardless of how simple it looks. PNG compresses the same image down to a fraction of that, which is why BMP survived only where compatibility matters more than size.

The pixels are copied unchanged - BMP does not compress and does not subsample colors. What you lose compared to the source PNG is only the alpha channel and, if the source was scaled before, whatever resampling already did.
Essentially all of them: Windows itself, most image editors, office suites and printing software. That reliability is the only reason to choose BMP over PNG or WebP.
